rows.notes: The study is a global literature review of 271 water accounts from 139 publications (Section 3 describes a systematic search of the SEEA website, WAVES knowledge base, Scopus and Google Scholar; Section 4 tabulates account producers, frameworks, frequency and content). It reports no own experiment, survey or measurement, so Q1 is no. It also contains nothing on flow metering networks linked to water-rights databases or on detecting illegal abstractions; the only related remarks are that water accounts use administrative data such as water licensing registers (Section 2.4) and the SEEA definition of consumption mentioning losses from illegal tapping and malfunctioning metering (Section 5.2), both descriptive rather than results. The passage's claim about metering linked to water rights is not evidenced here.
